extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or beginning graduate students studying algebraic topology
extracted.subtask_description: Introductory textbook treatment of the fundamental group: definitions (paths, loops, homotopy), construction of π1, basic properties, computations (π1(S1), product spaces, spheres), covering-space lifting techniques, and applications (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra, Brouwer, Borsuk–Ulam).

rubrics_metrics.name: Path (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A path in a space X is a continuous map f : I → X where I is the unit interval [0,1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endpoints f(0) and f(1) may be used to specify paths between points; paths are the basic objects to be deformed in homotopy. Example: linear homotopy in R^n shows any two paths with the same endpoints in a convex set are homotopic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy of paths (fixed-endpoint)
rubrics_metrics.description: A homotopy of paths in X is a family f_t : I → X, 0 ≤ t ≤ 1, such that (1) endpoints f_t(0)=x0 and f_t(1)=x1 are independent of t, and (2) the associated map F(s,t)=f_t(s) is continuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation f0 ≃ f1. This formalizes continuously deforming a path while keeping endpoints fixed. Used to define equivalence classes of paths; continuity on I×I is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy is an equivalence relation
rubrics_metrics.description: The relation of homotopy on paths with fixed endpoints is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses constant homotopy for reflexivity, time-reversal for symmetry, and concatenation/reparametrization for transitivity (construct homotopy by piecing together two homotopies on subintervals of t).

rubrics_metrics.name: Loop (definition) and basepoint
rubrics_metrics.description: A loop is a path f : I → X with f(0) = f(1) = x0; x0 is the basepoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loops based at x0 are the elements considered for π1(X,x0). All loops in a given path-component use the same basepoint up to isomorphism of π1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product (composition) of paths
rubrics_metrics.description: Given paths f,g with f(1)=g(0), the product f * g is the path traversing f then g, defined by f*g(s)=f(2s) for 0≤s≤1/2 and g(2s-1) for 1/2≤s≤1 (i.e., reparametrized to unit time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Composition respects homotopy classes: if f0 ≃ f1 and g0 ≃ g1 then f0*g0 ≃ f1*g1 (concatenate the homotopies). Product used to define group operation in π1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reparametrization preserves homotopy class
rubrics_metrics.description: A reparametrization f∘φ where φ : I→I is continuous with φ(0)=0 and φ(1)=1 preserves the homotopy class of f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use linear homotopy ϕ_t(s)=(1−t)φ(s)+t s to show fφ ≃ f; reparametrizations are frequently used to show associativity and identity properties (e.g., f*c ≃ f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental group π1(X,x0) (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: π1(X,x0) is the set of homotopy classes [f] of loops based at x0 with multiplication [f][g]=[f*g].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This set with the product induced by concatenation is a group (associativity up to homotopy, identity = constant loop, inverses = reverse paths). It is the primary algebraic invariant introduced in this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associativity of loop product (up to homotopy)
rubrics_metrics.description: For loops f,g,h the products (f*g)*h and f*(g*h) are homotopic; hence the product on π1 is associative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associativity is proven by showing one product is a reparametrization of the other (explicit piecewise-linear reparametrization φ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity and inverses in π1
rubrics_metrics.description: The homotopy class of the constant path at x0 is the identity; for a path f the inverse is f^−1(s)=f(1−s), and [f][f^−1] is homotopic to the constant loop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct explicit homotopies (described via a 'V'-shaped decomposition or time-dependent stationary intervals) to show concatenation with the reverse yields the constant loop up to homotopy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triviality of π1 in convex subsets of R^n (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a convex set X ⊂ R^n with basepoint x0, π1(X,x0)=0 because any two loops based at x0 are homotopic via linear homotopy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linear homotopy ft(s)=(1−t)f0(s)+t f1(s) stays inside convex X; demonstrates triviality of π1 in contractible/convex regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change-of-basepoint isomorphism β_h
rubrics_metrics.description: If h is a path from x0 to x1 then β_h : π1(X,x1)→π1(X,x0) is given by β_h([f])=[h*f*h^−1] and is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This implies π1(X,x0) is independent of basepoint up to isomorphism when X is path-connected; inverse is β_{h^−1} and homomorphism property follows from concatenation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simply-connected space (definition and equivalent condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A space X is simply-connected iff it is path-connected and π1(X) is trivial. Equivalently, there is a unique homotopy class of paths connecting any two points in X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of equivalence uses concatenation of paths and nullhomotopy of loops; simply-connectedness is the key obstruction-free condition for π1-based arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covering space (definition: evenly covered neighborhoods)
rubrics_metrics.description: A covering space p: X̃ → X satisfies: for each x∈X there is an open U such that p^{-1}(U) is a union of disjoint open sets each mapped homeomorphically onto U by p (U is evenly covered).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: p:R→S^1 given by p(s)=(cos 2πs, sin 2πs). Evenly covered arcs in S^1 lift to disjoint intervals in R; this structure underlies lifting lemmas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path lifting and homotopy lifting (uniqueness/existence)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For each path f : I→X starting at x0 and each x̃0 ∈ p^{-1}(x0) there is a unique lift f̃ : I→X̃ starting at x̃0. (b) Homotopies of paths lift uniquely given appropriate starting lifts. (c) General lifting lemma: maps F:Y×I→X lifting on Y×{0} extend uniquely to Y×I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These lifting properties are proven via evenly covered neighborhoods and compactness (partition interval into segments lying in evenly covered sets). They are the main technical tool to compute π1(S^1) and study covering spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation π1(S^1) ≅ Z (theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental group of the circle π1(S^1) is an infinite cyclic group generated by the homotopy class of ω(s)=(cos 2πs, sin 2πs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses covering map p:R→S^1 and path lifting: any loop lifts to a path in R starting at 0 and ending at an integer n, giving [f]=[ω^n]; uniqueness of n follows from uniqueness of lift endpoints. Interpret [ω]^n=[ω^n].

rubrics_metrics.name: Method: using covering-space lifts to compute π1
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare paths in X with paths in a covering space X̃ via a covering map p; lift loops and read off algebraic data (like winding numbers) from endpoints of lifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This general strategy is illustrated by the S^1 calculation (lift to R) and is applicable in broader contexts. The general lifting lemma (c) is the technical backbone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: Fundamental Theorem of Algebra via π1(S^1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a complex polynomial p(z) had no roots, one constructs loops f_r(s)=p(r e^{2π i s})/|p(r e^{2π i s})| in S^1 that vary continuously with r; for large r f_r is homotopic to ω^n, contradicting nullhomotopy when r→0, hence polynomial has a root.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key idea: use homotopy of loops on S^1 and the calculation π1(S^1)≅Z to derive contradiction; choose r large enough so polynomial behaves like z^n on |z|=r.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: Brouwer fixed point theorem (2D) via π1
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume continuous h:D^2→D^2 has no fixed point; define retraction r(x) to S^1 by shooting ray from h(x) through x; r is continuous and equals identity on S^1, giving a retraction D^2→S^1 and contradicting nontrivial π1(S^1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how nonexistence of certain maps (retractions) can be ruled out by π1 computations. Relies on the fact π1(D^2)=0 but π1(S^1)≈Z.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application: Borsuk–Ulam theorem (n=2) via lifting argument
rubrics_metrics.description: For continuous f:S^2→R^2, assume no antipodal pair maps equally and define g(x)=(f(x)-f(-x))/|f(x)-f(-x)|:S^2→S^1; composing with equatorial loop and lifting yields an odd winding number contradicting nullhomotopy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses parity/oddness obtained from lift endpoints (integer degree) and the fact equator loop is nullhomotopic in S^2 but its image under g would be non-null in S^1, contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product spaces: π1(X×Y) ≅ π1(X)×π1(Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are path-connected then π1(X×Y) is isomorphic to π1(X)×π1(Y) via [f]↦([proj_X∘f],[proj_Y∘f]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity criterion for product maps yields correspondence between loops/homotopies in product and pairs of loops/homotopies in factors. Example: torus S^1×S^1 has π1≅Z×Z and loops (p,q)-windings correspond to torus knots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Induced homomorphism ϕ_* (functoriality)
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuous map ϕ:(X,x0)→(Y,y0) induces ϕ_*:π1(X,x0)→π1(Y,y0) by ϕ_*([f])=[ϕ∘f]. Functorial properties: (ϕ∘ψ)_*=ϕ_*∘ψ_* and id_* = id.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Induced maps transform topological relations into algebraic ones; homeomorphisms induce isomorphisms on π1 via this construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: π1(S^n)=0 for n≥2 (calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: For n≥2 the fundamental group π1(S^n) is trivial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses covering the sphere by two open sets each homeomorphic to R^n whose intersection is path-connected (for n≥2), then Lemma 1.15 shows any loop decomposes into loops in R^n factors which are nullhomotopic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma on decomposing loops via open cover (Lemma 1.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is union of path-connected open sets A_α each containing basepoint x0 and each intersection A_α∩A_β is path-connected, then every loop at x0 is homotopic to a product of loops each contained in a single A_α.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: partition I so each piece maps into some A_α, then insert connector paths g_i in intersections to rewrite f as concatenation of loops lying in single A_α. This lemma is used to reduce global loops to local pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using π1 to distinguish non-homeomorphic spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Homeomorphic spaces have isomorphic fundamental groups; thus non-isomorphic π1 groups imply spaces are not homeomorphic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: R^2−{0} has π1≈Z while R^n−{x} has trivial π1 for n>2, so R^2 is not homeomorphic to R^n for n≠2. More generally, π1 is a computable invariant for distinguishing spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction and deformation retract implications on π1
rubrics_metrics.description: If X retracts onto A then inclusion-induced map i_*:π1(A)→π1(X) is injective. If A is a deformation retract of X then i_* is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: retraction r satisfies r∘i=id so r_*∘i_*=id on π1(A) implying injectivity; deformation retraction gives surjectivity by homotoping loops into A. Use this to rule out certain retractions (e.g., S^1↛D^2).
